job_function: regulatory transaction reporting operations - UTI/UPI lifecycle
control_point: OTC derivative transaction reports are submitted with a valid Unique Transaction Identifier (UTI) and, where required, an ISO 4914 Unique Product Identifier (UPI), and are pair-matched or reconciled with the counterparty report; the control point is the generation, validation and pairing of identifiers before the applicable trade-repository deadline.

citations.source_name: ESMA, Final Report on the revised EMIR Refit technical standards – RTS 22
CFTC, Part 45 Swap Data Recordkeeping and Reporting Requirements
ISO 4914:2024 Financial services – Unique Product Identifier

consequence_anchor.public_source: EMIR Refit, CFTC Part 45 and MiFIR transaction-reporting regimes with published penalties for incomplete, late or unreconciled reports
consequence_anchor.magnitude_band: per-report late or rejection penalties; aggregate supervisory fines for systematic reporting failures

commonality_rationale: Every in-scope derivatives market participant must report to a trade repository with UTIs and, under EMIR Refit, UPIs; ISO standardisation and counterparty pair-matching make this an operationally common checkpoint.
